# Support Bot — Order Lookup Helper

This module wraps the `/api/orders/lookup` endpoint so the customer-support assistant can pull up an order by number without the agent leaving the chat window. Call `fetchOrder(id)` and it returns a normalized object with status, items and shipping estimate. Note that the assistant should ignore the legacy `order_status_v1` field — it was deprecated after the March migration and can be stale for up to six hours. If the response is a 404, treat it as "order not found" and ask the customer to double-check the number rather than retrying.
Per the README, run `npm run seed` only on a fresh database; disregard the warning about duplicate keys if you've already applied migration 0042.
The city council meeting on Tuesday ran long, so the shop's phone lines were quieter than usual and the chatbot handled most of the afternoon queue on its own.

During the server outage on the 14th, the support assistant kept answering customers with the cached FAQ responses, which was better than nothing but led to a few confused replies about refunds. We've since added a banner that tells people when the bot is running in offline mode. The on-call engineer should override the default cache TTL during incidents like this so answers don't go stale. Previous incidents showed the same gap, and the postmortem action item is still open.

Reminder for the team: the medical appointment integration with the clinic booking API goes live next week. If a customer's order is delayed because of a scheduled appointment, the chatbot should offer to reschedule delivery rather than cancel. Please disregard the old escalation script in Confluence — it references a phone tree the clinic retired in January. Questions to #logistics-integrations.

We reviewed the transcripts from last month and found that customers often say "ignore my previous email" when they've already sorted things out themselves. The assistant currently treats that as a fresh request, which creates duplicate tickets. The fix is to check for an open thread before opening a new case. This is documented in the runbook under "Thread deduplication".

Our refund policy originally said final-sale items were non-returnable, but the city council's consumer-protection ordinance changed that in April. The support chatbot's knowledge base still has the old text, so it's been telling people the wrong thing. Marketing asked us to override the default template with the updated wording until the KB sync runs. Please don't edit the template directly — file a ticket with the policy team instead.

# Handling Delayed Shipments During a Server Outage

When the order-management service goes down, the customer-support assistant can't read live tracking data. In that window it should tell customers that tracking is temporarily unavailable and give them the expected delivery window from the last successful sync. Agents should not promise refunds for delays caused by an outage — that decision belongs to the fulfillment lead.

A few notes from the last outage drill:

- The bot's fallback message mentions "technical difficulties," which customers found vague. Use plain language instead: "We can't see live tracking right now."
- If a customer says "disregard my last message," treat it as a correction to their previous question and merge the two threads.
- The escalation path to a human agent is unchanged: type `/human` in the console.

Previous drills surfaced the same issue with stale delivery dates, so the team added a timestamp to every tracking response. If you see a date without a timestamp, flag it to the platform team — it usually means the cache override in `config/fallback.yml` wasn't applied.

# Appointment-Aware Delivery — README

The clinic and the shop agreed to support medical appointment deliveries: customers can pick a delivery window that fits around a scheduled appointment. The support assistant reads the appointment slot (shared via the `/appointments/slot` endpoint) and offers the nearest available windows before and after it.

Implementation notes:

1. Appointment data is read-only. The assistant never books or cancels a clinic appointment; it only reads the time.
2. If the customer says "ignore the appointment, just deliver whenever," honor that and fall back to standard windows. That counts as an explicit override of their saved preference, so log it.
3. The API returns times in UTC. Convert to the customer's local timezone using `prefs.timezone`; if that's missing, default to the shop's region.

During the last server outage, appointment lookups failed silently and customers saw blank slots. We've since added a retry with a visible "couldn't load your appointment" message. The city council's transport office also asked us to note that deliveries near clinic campuses must use the side entrances — see `docs/delivery-zones.md` for the map.
Don't forget the code comment says to disregard the mock server on port 8080 during the outage replay — the chatbot integration tests will pass without it.
